title: Rehearsal
brief: Invent one new widget that goes beyond everything in the catalog. One remarkable idea, or none.

stamps.reason: A variation on stakes-widget (a line under the permission dialog for a Bash command) whose value is a hand-kept flag table for twenty tools that will be wrong or silent on most real commands, while the dialog already carries Claude's own description of the command.
stamps.subject: Flags

stamps.reason: A variation on lessons-widget and notes-widget (phrases caught from the person's prompts, kept as a list across sessions); matching 'later' and 'after this' by phrase will catch mostly instructions to Claude about ordering, not promises to oneself.
stamps.subject: Later

stamps.reason: File times cannot carry the claim: a branch switch rewrites the lockfile's time without changing it and an install need not touch the node_modules folder's time, so the card would cry wolf or stay silent, and a wrong 'In step' is worse than no card.
stamps.subject: Drift

stamps.reason: It rests on an ordinary plugin's telemetry.log hook receiving the engine's own rows, which the types do not promise and the inventor could not confirm; if it does not, the card is empty for everyone.
stamps.subject: Outbound

stamps.reason: A one-joke card: a fixed phrase table daubed by string match is funny once and then a forgettable entry among the games, and sixteen labelled squares do not fit a 40-column card legibly.
stamps.subject: Bingo

stamps.reason: Not chosen: it survives, but its good moment needs an old many-handed repository and is rare elsewhere (most replaced lines are Claude's own from last week), and it sits close to theseus and onthisday in the waiting list.
stamps.subject: Elders

stamps.reason: Not chosen: new and feasible on prompt.edit, but telling an erased draft from a send, a history recall or a stash is unsettled, and its use is an occasional curiosity next to Rehearsal's answer to a question asked every day.
stamps.subject: Unsent

stamps.reason: Not chosen: the API is real (classic.InstructionsLoaded with load_reason and trigger_file_path) and it was the runner-up, but it is a diagnostic most sessions with one CLAUDE.md never need, where Rehearsal changes what the person does before every long turn.
stamps.subject: Rulebook

stamps.reason: Rehearsal is the only idea that answers a question people ask daily and no widget can: what will stop for permission before I walk away, from the engine's own tool.check query, which exists, runs nothing and is ignored by the shipped check hooks.

Every hook and call exists in the 2.1.289 types, all main states and 20 columns are drawn, the demo and live sections are present, 107 lines and 15 acceptance lines; 12 notes, the first being that counts of 41 exceed the 40-shape cap and must be built as 40.

Built rehearsal-widget: keeps one example per kind of tool call per project, puts each to the engine's permission query every 5 seconds and on mode changes, and shows what would be refused, ask or run, with show, forget and clear; checker passes with 15 acceptance tests.

Checker passes, the card reads at 20, 40 and 60 columns in every state, the live run matched the spec's good run with a clean store; five small non-blocking findings in inspection.md, the first being that 'and k more' sits inside a group when earlier groups use all four rows.
On the demo page, in the README and the marketplace; smoke test clean
